items.title: MPs vote to reject revised assisted dying bill
items.summary: MPs have voted against revised proposals to legalise assisted dying in England and Wales that would have allowed nurses to be involved in parts of the proposed process. The Terminally Ill Adults (End of Life) Bill failed to progress beyond its second reading in the House of Commons last week, with MPs voting by 286...

items.title: MPs reject revived assisted dying bill in ‘incredibly close’ vote
items.summary: MPs have voted against the revived assisted dying bill in its second reading in the House of Commons today.

items.title: Assisted dying bill could expose GPs to discrimination by future employers, BMA warns
items.summary: The assisted dying bill could expose GPs to discrimination by future employers, the BMA has warned. In a briefing on the bill, which is returning to Parliament tomorrow, the union urged MPs to amend the legislation to ensure that protection from discrimination extends to job applicants.

items.title: District nurse shortages ‘contributing’ to end-of-life care being given in hospital corridors
items.summary: A shortage of district nurses means vulnerable people approaching the end of their life are being hospitalised and, in some cases, cared for in corridors, the Royal College of Nursing (RCN) has warned.

items.title: Assisted dying – more training required
items.summary: Copperfield utters the sentence he never thought he would: when it comes to assisted dying, GPs do in fact need more mandatory training Quiz time. What’s one of the most annoying impositions in primary care? Correct: ‘mandatory’ training. And why is it so irritating?

items.title: QICN faculty to support nurses working in palliative and end of life care
items.summary: The Queen’s Institute of Community Nursing (QICN) has launched a new faculty for community nurses working in palliative and end of life care settings – its ninth and final faculty aimed at supporting the profession in different fields of nursing.
